title: Source layers
summary: A fixed copy of the UN Geodata 2023 polygons and lines, the GAUL 2025 polygons and cells, and the FieldMaps cells, plus the land GAUL and UN Geodata polygons give to different entities.
why: Everything after this point can be traced back to these files.

title: Split into parts
summary: Each UN Geodata row is separated into its individual polygons, so every island and mainland can be handled alone.
why: An island can belong to a different GAUL entity than the mainland of the same UN row.

title: Cut the mainlands
summary: Mainland parts are cut where GAUL has an entity that UN Geodata 2023 draws inside a neighbour. UN lines are used where they exist. GAUL lines are used for the India-China areas, where UN has none.
why: Each disputed area becomes a separate piece, so keeping or dissolving it stays an open choice.

title: Attribute to GAUL
summary: Every piece is given a GAUL entity as a whole, so an island is never divided. A piece takes the GAUL entity its UN entity links to in gaul_links, unless island_overrides gives it to another entity for a listed change.
why: GAUL keeps all of its entities but follows UN Geodata's ownership, so a piece moves only through a listed change, such as the islands off the Hala'ib coast.

title: Units and crosswalk
summary: Pieces with the same UN entity and GAUL entity are grouped into units. The crosswalk links each unit to both sources, and every change is listed.
why: The units are the build layer, and the crosswalk lets it produce either export.

title: Exports and checks
summary: The units are dissolved by UN key and by GAUL key, then compared with the sources.
why: The units still add up to every UN Geodata 2023 row, and every GAUL entity and code is kept.

title: Extend into water
summary: The units grow outward into the surrounding water to form cells that cover the whole map. A coastline can then be applied as a final clip.
why: Cells keep the political divisions separate from the coastline, so a land source can be chosen later.

title: Site files
summary: Map tiles and tables for the build page, built from the earlier stages.
why: The page shows exactly what the stages produced.
